name: git-avoid-sweeping-operations
description: Blocks git commands that act on everything they can reach instead of named paths and refs. Complements CC Safety Net's built-in git rules (reset --hard, clean -f, branch -D, push --force, stash drop/clear, checkout/restore of the worktree). The why and the alternatives live in the git-hygiene-avoid-sweeping-operations skill. Gaps: a value-taking global option such as `git -C <dir>` hides the subcommand, so `git -C repo add -A` isn't caught; bare `git reset` and `git checkout <branch>` in a shared checkout aren't expressible as exact-token matches; combined short options are listed explicitly because version 2 doesn't expand them.
author: nhooey/git-skills

rules.name: add-sweep
rules.reason: Stages every change in the tree, including others' edits and untracked files. Run `git add <paths>` or `git add -p <paths>`.

rules.name: commit-all
rules.reason: Commits every tracked change, staged or not. Run `git add <paths>`, then `git commit`.

rules.name: stash-sweep
rules.reason: Stashes every change in the tree, others' included. Run `git stash push -- <paths>`, or use a separate worktree.

rules.name: restore-staged-sweep
rules.reason: Acts on every path anyone staged or changed. Run `git restore --staged <paths>` or `git restore <paths>` for the paths you changed.

rules.name: push-all-refs
rules.reason: Pushes every local branch or tag, scratch ones included. Run `git push origin <branch>` or `git push origin <tag>`.

rules.name: commit-no-verify
rules.reason: Skips the repo's commit hooks. Fix what the hook reports instead.

rules.name: push-no-verify
rules.reason: Skips the repo's pre-push hooks. Fix what the hook reports instead.

rules.name: worktree-prune
rules.reason: Prunes other sessions' worktree records. Run `git worktree remove <path>` for worktrees you created.

rules.name: gc-prune-now
rules.reason: Deletes unreachable commits, the recovery net for every other mistake. Leave gc to git's defaults.

rules.name: reflog-expire
rules.reason: Expires the reflog, the recovery net for every other mistake. Leave it to git's defaults.

rules.name: config-global-write
rules.reason: Changes git settings for every repo on the machine. Use `git config --local`, or ask the user first.
